migration_id_rule: 14-digit UTC timestamp, underscore, then a lowercase kebab-case slug; an ID is never reused and is never renamed in place.
canonical_path_rule: The canonical_directory is fixed to db/migrations (any other declared value is rejected). A canonical migration exists exactly at db/migrations/<migration_id>.sql as a single direct child; nested directories, dot segments, duplicate slashes, other directories, other extensions, traversal, absolute paths, duplicate paths, or a basename that does not equal the ID are rejected.
ordering_rule: The migrations array is strictly ascending by migration ID; duplicate IDs, duplicate paths, and timestamp reversal are rejected.
checksum_byte_rule: Checksum is SHA-256 over the raw bytes of the SQL file with no newline, whitespace, comment, or BOM normalization; any byte change (LF/CRLF, trailing newline, trailing space, comment, BOM, single byte) fails closed. An applied migration is never edited; a correction is a new forward-fix migration.
activation_rule: No existing scripts are retroactively declared applied. A separately approved adoption baseline must be attested before this manifest changes to ACTIVE.
destructive_ddl_rule: A canonical migration containing destructive DDL must set risk_class=DESTRUCTIVE, declare the full set of statically detected destructive operations from the fixed operation vocabulary (no partial, unknown, duplicate, or spurious declaration), and carry a non-empty, non-placeholder approval reference. Missing, partial, unknown, spurious, or placeholder-approved declarations fail closed.
